Although completion of the coursework listed below is not necessarily mandatory prior to admission, students are strongly advised to complete as much lower-division course preparation as possible prior to transfer. This agreement does not contain upper-division (junior-senior) major requirements, general education, or all-university requirements necessary for completion of this degree. In some cases, there may be alternative course options at the upper-division level. Please review the CSUSB catalog for full details. TRANSFER ADMISSION INFORMATION You can find information about admission to CSUSB as a transfer student here: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students TRANSFER SUCCESS PATHWAY Enrolling in the Transfer Success Pathway provides you with dual admission to a California Community College and a specific CSU campus. The TSP ensures a more streamlined transfer experience since you can choose the specific community college courses that will apply to your intended major at your destination CSU campus. See if you qualify for the Transfer Success Pathway here: https://www.calstate.edu/apply/transfer/Pages/transfer-success-pathway.aspx FINANCIAL AID Students who plan to transfer directly from a California Community College to a 4-year university can apply for the Cal Grant Transfer Entitlement Award. The application deadline is March 2nd each year, and students must submit a FAFSA or CA Dream Act Application. The minimum GPA is a 2.40. More information is available here: https://www.csac.ca.gov/post/cal-grant-transfer-entitlement-award ASSOCIATE DEGREES FOR TRANSFER (ADTs) A complete list of CSUSB majors/concentrations that are similar to the Associate Degrees for Transfer (ADTs) can be found here: https://www.csusb.edu/registrar/articulation/associate-degree-transfer Students who intend to transfer to CSUSB with the ADT guarantee MUST submit final transcripts with the earned ADT recorded by the final document deadline: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students/transfer-deadlines Students who submit transcripts after the document deadline are NOT guaranteed to graduate within 60 semester units. EXPLORE MAJORS AND CAREERS The CSUSB Career Center has collected a variety of resources to help students choose or confirm their major and explore different career paths: https://www.csusb.edu/career-center/students/career-resources/major-and-career-exploration TEST CREDIT If you took an AP, IB, or CLEP test, you can look up your CSUSB credit here: https://www.csusb.edu/registrar/articulation/test-credit TRANSFER HELP Do you have questions about your transfer work? Need some guidance? You can talk with one of our Transfer and Graduation Counselors! Email: transferhelp@csusb.edu Phone: 909-537-5200, Option 4 Zoom: Set up an appointment by emailing transferhelp@csusb.edu You are also welcome to visit us in person. We are located in the Office of the Registrar , on the first floor of University Hall ( interactive map link ).

This agreement displays only the lower-division courses required in the major. Although completion of the coursework listed below is not necessarily mandatory prior to admission, students are strongly advised to complete as much lower-division course preparation as possible prior to transfer. This agreement does not contain upper-division (junior-senior) major requirements, general education, or all-university requirements necessary for completion of this degree. In some cases, there may be alternative course options at the upper-division level. Please review the CSUSB catalog for full details.


TRANSFER ADMISSION INFORMATION

You can find information about admission to CSUSB as a transfer student here: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students


TRANSFER SUCCESS PATHWAY

Enrolling in the Transfer Success Pathway provides you with dual admission to a California Community College and a specific CSU campus. The TSP ensures a more streamlined transfer experience since you can choose the specific community college courses that will apply to your intended major at your destination CSU campus. See if you qualify for the Transfer Success Pathway here: https://www.calstate.edu/apply/transfer/Pages/transfer-success-pathway.aspx


FINANCIAL AID

Students who plan to transfer directly from a California Community College to a 4-year university can apply for the Cal Grant Transfer Entitlement Award. The application deadline is March 2nd each year, and students must submit a FAFSA or CA Dream Act Application. The minimum GPA is a 2.40. More information is available here: https://www.csac.ca.gov/post/cal-grant-transfer-entitlement-award


ASSOCIATE DEGREES FOR TRANSFER (ADTs)

A complete list of CSUSB majors/concentrations that are similar to the Associate Degrees for Transfer (ADTs) can be found here: https://www.csusb.edu/registrar/articulation/associate-degree-transfer

Students who intend to transfer to CSUSB with the ADT guarantee MUST submit final transcripts with the earned ADT recorded by the final document deadline: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students/transfer-deadlines

Students who submit transcripts after the document deadline are NOT guaranteed to graduate within 60 semester units.


EXPLORE MAJORS AND CAREERS

  • The CSUSB Career Center has collected a variety of resources to help students choose or confirm their major and explore different career paths: https://www.csusb.edu/career-center/students/career-resources/major-and-career-exploration


TEST CREDIT

If you took an AP, IB, or CLEP test, you can look up your CSUSB credit here: https://www.csusb.edu/registrar/articulation/test-credit


TRANSFER HELP

Do you have questions about your transfer work? Need some guidance? You can talk with one of our Transfer and Graduation Counselors!

  • Email: transferhelp@csusb.edu
  • Phone: 909-537-5200, Option 4
  • Zoom: Set up an appointment by emailing transferhelp@csusb.edu

You are also welcome to visit us in person. We are located in the Office of the Registrar, on the first floor of University Hall (interactive map link).

notes.content: CONCENTRATIONS Students in this major are required to choose one of the following concentrations: Pre-credential General Pre-credential Spanish Studies Credential - Integrated MAJOR INFORMATION The BA in Liberal Studies major is designed to prepare students for Multiple-Subject Teaching Credential Programs in California. The core of the program has four areas: Arts and Humanities, Natural Sciences and Mathematics, Social Sciences and Child Development, and Program Requirements. These areas are designed to provide students with coursework that is both foundational and focused. The first three areas – Arts and Humanities, Natural Sciences and Mathematics, Social Sciences and Child Development – enable students to build a broad repertoire of knowledge in the arts, humanities, natural and social sciences, technology, and civics and government. These areas of knowledge ensure a well-rounded education for students; they also provide the content of what they will teach in California’s K-8 schools. The program requirements include courses on learning assessment and metaknowledge of their studies and chosen careers. Unless otherwise specified, grades in lower division courses (2999 and below) must be a "C-" or better; grades in upper division courses (3000 and above) must be a "C" or better. All graduating Liberal Studies students must maintain a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 2.0 ("C"). Students who plan to seek their Multiple Subject Teaching Credential at CSUSB must achieve a minimum GPA of 2.67. Other institutions offering Multiple Subject Teaching Credentials may have different GPA requirements, usually between 2.5 to 3.0. The Pre-Credential General Concentration is intended for students who wish to pursue a Multiple-Subject Teaching Credential after graduation. The Pre-Credential Spanish Studies Concentration is designed for those students interested in the Bilingual Added Authorization in the Multiple-Subject Teaching Credential program, which gives them the eligibility to teach in a bilingual/Spanish classroom setting. The Credential-Integrated Concentration includes all the courses in the CSUSB Multiple-Subject Credential program and generally requires an additional semester to complete. ALL MAJOR REQUIREMENTS The complete list of major requirements is available here: https://catalog.csusb.edu/colleges-schools-departments/arts-letters/liberal-studies-office/liberal-studies-ba/ The lower-division General Education requirements can be completed with any California Community College transfer GE pattern. CSUSB ADVISING PODCASTS Find out more about this major here: What is the Liberal Studies Major? ASSOCIATE DEGREE FOR TRANSFER (ADTs) The Pre-Credential General Concentration is similar to the Associate Degree for Transfer (ADT) in Elementary Teacher Education: Integrated Programs. The other two concentrations are not similar. HOWEVER, the articulation agreement below represents the straightest pathway through the major. All of the requirements below must be completed for this degree, whether an ADT has been earned or not. Completion of the ADT guarantees that students will be able to graduate from a similar-designated major at CSUSB in no more than 60 semester units. The ADT does not guarantee that all lower-division requirements are met. Community college transfer students with a compatible ADT MUST meet with an academic advisor early in their first term and each subsequent term to stay on track for graduation.

CONCENTRATIONS

Students in this major are required to choose one of the following concentrations:

  • Pre-credential General
  • Pre-credential Spanish Studies
  • Credential - Integrated


MAJOR INFORMATION

The BA in Liberal Studies major is designed to prepare students for Multiple-Subject Teaching Credential Programs in California.


The core of the program has four areas: Arts and Humanities, Natural Sciences and Mathematics, Social Sciences and Child Development, and Program Requirements.

These areas are designed to provide students with coursework that is both foundational and focused. The first three areas – Arts and Humanities, Natural Sciences and Mathematics, Social Sciences and Child Development – enable students to build a broad repertoire of knowledge in the arts, humanities, natural and social sciences, technology, and civics and government. These areas of knowledge ensure a well-rounded education for students; they also provide the content of what they will teach in California’s K-8 schools. The program requirements include courses on learning assessment and metaknowledge of their studies and chosen careers.


Unless otherwise specified, grades in lower division courses (2999 and below) must be a "C-" or better; grades in upper division courses (3000 and above) must be a "C" or better.

All graduating Liberal Studies students must maintain a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 2.0 ("C"). Students who plan to seek their Multiple Subject Teaching Credential at CSUSB must achieve a minimum GPA of 2.67. Other institutions offering Multiple Subject Teaching Credentials may have different GPA requirements, usually between 2.5 to 3.0.


The Pre-Credential General Concentration is intended for students who wish to pursue a Multiple-Subject Teaching Credential after graduation.

The Pre-Credential Spanish Studies Concentration is designed for those students interested in the Bilingual Added Authorization in the Multiple-Subject Teaching Credential program, which gives them the eligibility to teach in a bilingual/Spanish classroom setting.

The Credential-Integrated Concentration includes all the courses in the CSUSB Multiple-Subject Credential program and generally requires an additional semester to complete.


ALL MAJOR REQUIREMENTS

The complete list of major requirements is available here: https://catalog.csusb.edu/colleges-schools-departments/arts-letters/liberal-studies-office/liberal-studies-ba/

The lower-division General Education requirements can be completed with any California Community College transfer GE pattern.


CSUSB ADVISING PODCASTS

Find out more about this major here:

  • What is the Liberal Studies Major?


ASSOCIATE DEGREE FOR TRANSFER (ADTs)

The Pre-Credential General Concentration is similar to the Associate Degree for Transfer (ADT) in Elementary Teacher Education: Integrated Programs. The other two concentrations are not similar.

HOWEVER, the articulation agreement below represents the straightest pathway through the major. All of the requirements below must be completed for this degree, whether an ADT has been earned or not.


Completion of the ADT guarantees that students will be able to graduate from a similar-designated major at CSUSB in no more than 60 semester units. The ADT does not guarantee that all lower-division requirements are met.


Community college transfer students with a compatible ADT MUST meet with an academic advisor early in their first term and each subsequent term to stay on track for graduation.
